notes: Boundary edges for every numeric law the workflow owns. Text byte counts are UTF-8 byte counts, never code-unit or code-point counts.
LIM-005 pins the arithmetic relation that makes marker overflow unreachable by construction: the E1 marker cap equals the domain chord-event cap plus the domain section cap.

LIM-007 pins the accessibility matrix completeness obligation: every workflow state crossed with every overlay surface has exactly one row carrying initial focus, allowed actions, focus return, and announcement key.

cases.summary: A marker text of exactly 96 UTF-8 bytes is kept.
A marker text of 97 UTF-8 bytes is omitted with text-over-limit; a marker is never truncated.
A marker text containing one ASCII control character is omitted with text-control-chars regardless of length.
A title of exactly 96 UTF-8 bytes is exported verbatim with no notice.
A 97-byte title of thirty-two sharp signs plus one ASCII letter truncates to exactly the thirty-two sharps (96 bytes): truncation never splits a code point and never exceeds the byte cap.
A title with any ASCII control character is replaced by the pinned fallback with the substitution notice; user text is never repaired character-by-character.
Marker-cap arithmetic: maxChordEvents + maxSections equals maxMarkers exactly, so derivation overflow is unreachable by construction.
Preparation-id brand bounds: 1 and 2^53-1 are constructible; 0, 2^53, negatives, and non-integers are not.
Accessibility matrix completeness: 6 workflow states × 2 overlay surfaces = 12 rows, each carrying the frozen row vocabulary.
Filename truncation edge from the E1 law: a document id that would push the name past 64 characters is truncated so the whole name, including .mid, fits.
